newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks fall back to earth by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks fall back to earth by close.

text.p: SPI futures 2451 -3 US 30yr cl 6.70 -0.06
10yrbond futs 92.585 steady Gold NY 341.75 Lon fix 340.90
*Stocks end flat, tumbling from early record highs as miners lead way down from peak in light trade. Volume 355.13 million, value A$605.14 million, 1,126 stocks traded, 334 steady, 415 up, 377 down.
A mixed Australian share market fell back to earth in the afternoon to close little changed on Monday after a slow, choppy day's trade.
Having scaled fresh heights early, the thin market tumbled back down the mountain just as quickly as the miners were mauled on concerns over commodity prices and the Australian dollar.

By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 0.3 points lower at 2,446.4 after hitting an intraday and record high of 2,461.9, surpassing the previous record of 2,456.7 on January 20. March share index futures were down three points at 2,451, a 4.6 point premium to the index.

"I was bullish this morning and that was borne out by the early events but the major resources stocks led it down in the afternoon," said broker Kevin Lourey of Melbourne-based brokerage, Peake Lands Kirwan.
"It would appear the market is not so sure about the strength of our dollar and also about commodity prices."
Other players echoed similar sentiments about a start that promised so much but failed to deliver.
"It came right off the top after running hard early," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding that only modest investor interest had made it difficult to convincingly capture the early heights.
"There was not much trade though and not enough interest to keep it at the higher levels. Many are still waiting to see the upcoming profit results," he said.
Miner CRA underpinned the market's early ascent and held most of its gains to limit the day's overall losses.

Other resource stocks failed to fare as well. Major oil producers Woodside Petroleum and Santos Ltd came under pressure from the sharp fall in the oil price with both their shares closing about 2.5 percent lower at A$9.40 and A$4.71 respectively.

In the industrials, the banks continued to be the feature and Commonwealth Bank the star player. Its shares closed 12 cents higher at A$13.58 after reaching a record high of A$13.78 on profit expectations from its half year results due Wednesday, its continuing yield attraction and persistent speculation about a special dividend.
Major brewing group Foster's Brewing closed 11 cents lower at A$2.54 despite a 13 percent higher first half pre-tax operating profit of A$184.8 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 10 to nine, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives was at only moderate levels.
Total options traded 33,722 (32,174)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 5,659 (4,257)

In other local markets, Australian bonds were limited to a relatively narrow trading range ahead of Tuesday's A$900 million two-tranche Treasury bond tender with the longer of the two expected to see keen interest.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.36 percent, down from Friday's 7.38 percent.
The Australian dollar idled through a quiet day, content to watch the gyrations of the U.S. dollar as the market reacted to the G7's statement on foreign exchange values.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the dollar was at US$0.7599/04, from an an early US$0.7599/04 and US$0.7605/10 her Friday.
